Creates a new rigid body from the geometry of an entity and returns it. The entity itself is left as it is: it does not become a body, and stays where it is. To show it with the body, make it a child of the body, keeping its place: `EntityParent mesh, body, True`.

The size and turn of the entity in the world are used. Shapes: `0` automatic (a triangle mesh for static and kinematic bodies, a convex hull for dynamic ones), `1` the box that holds the mesh, `3` the ellipsoid that holds that box, `4` the convex hull of the mesh (of up to 126 corners that were picked to keep its outline) and `5` a triangle mesh, which is exact but can only be static or kinematic. A box and an ellipsoid are placed around the middle of the mesh, so the body is not at the origin of the entity; a hull and a mesh are at the origin. The body starts with a mass of 1 kilogram.

```blitzbasic
rock = LoadMesh("rock.b3d")
PositionEntity rock, 0, 6, 0
body = CreatePhysicsBodyFromEntity(rock, 3, 4)
EntityParent rock, body, True
```
@param entity The entity to read the geometry of. A terrain and a mesh without triangles can not be used.
@param motion 1 static, 2 kinematic, 3 dynamic.
@param shape 0, 1, 3, 4 or 5, see above.
@param world The physics world, 0 (default) for the default world.
@returns The body, which is an entity.
@gap The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
